TIME-WINDOW CONVENTIONS: When a task specifies a time period, interpret its boundaries as follows (unless the task explicitly states otherwise), so your figures cover exactly the intended readings:
- A day, a date range, a month or a year means whole days. In the air-quality records (`df`, `cities_df`) hour h is the hour ENDING at h:00, so a day is its hours 1 to 23 and hour 0 of the next date, and a period runs from just after its first instant to its last instant inclusive; the reanalysis records are instants and a day is their hours 0 to 23 (see TIMESTAMPS in the schema notes below).
- An explicit clock range ("HH:MM to HH:MM", or two datetimes "T1 to T2") is start-inclusive and end-exclusive: include readings at or after the start time and STRICTLY before the end time.
- An "N-hour period ending at T" (e.g. "the 24 hours ending 2025-07-02 15:00") is end-inclusive: include the reading at T and the preceding N-1 hourly readings; the reading exactly N hours before T is NOT included.

DATA GRANULARITY: Unless a task explicitly asks for a separately-reported daily/official index or a pre-aggregated record, compute every period statistic (mean, total, peak, count, standard deviation, etc.) from the HOURLY readings in that period. For example, a period "mean AQI" is the arithmetic average of the hourly AQI values over the period, NOT a separately-reported daily AQI figure (these differ because such indices are non-linear).

<dataset_schema>
The dataset is a pandas DataFrame named `df` containing hourly air quality observations
from 12 national monitoring stations in Beijing, China. Time range: 2020-01-01 to 2026-07-20.
The network publishes no meteorology, so `df` has none — use `met_df` / `profile_df` for weather.

Columns:
  No        int     — Row index number
  year      int     — Year (2020-2026)
  month     int     — Month (1-12)
  day       int     — Day of month (1-31)
  hour      int     — Hour label (0-23): the hour ENDING at this time; 0 is 24:00 of the previous date
  PM2.5     float   — PM2.5 concentration (ug/m3)
  PM10      float   — PM10 concentration (ug/m3)
  SO2       float   — SO2 concentration (ug/m3)
  NO2       float   — NO2 concentration (ug/m3)
  CO        float   — CO concentration (ug/m3)
  O3        float   — O3 concentration (ug/m3)

  station   str     — Station name
  station_code str   — Station code (e.g. '1001A')
  longitude float    — Station longitude (°E)
  latitude  float    — Station latitude (°N)

Two auxiliary DataFrames are also pre-registered in the runtime:

`pop_df` — pandas DataFrame (~7MB) of Beijing population at 100 m grid resolution.
  Columns:
    longitude  float — Grid cell centre longitude (°E)
    latitude   float — Grid cell centre latitude (°N)
    population float — People per 100×100 m cell
  Use haversine distance for spatial queries; ~329k rows covering the Beijing area.
  Cells are nominally 100 m x 100 m; their coordinate spacing is ~0.00089 deg, so a
  cell measures about 76 m east-west at this latitude. Treat a cell as 100 m x 100 m
  (0.01 km2) when converting counts to densities unless a question says otherwise.

`poi_df` — pandas DataFrame (~720KB) of Beijing points of interest from OpenStreetMap.
  Columns:
    name  str — POI name
    lon   float — Longitude (°E)
    lat   float — Latitude (°N)
    type  str — POI type; one of: school, residential, park, industrial,
                kindergarten, hospital, university, pharmacy, community_centre,
                playground, clinic, social_facility

`met_df` — pandas DataFrame of ERA5 reanalysis surface meteorology, one row per station-hour,
  timestamps in Beijing local time (join on year/month/day/hour/station).
  Columns: datetime, year, month, day, hour, station
    blh_m — planetary boundary layer height (m)
    wind_speed_ms, wind_dir_deg — 10 m wind; direction is where the wind blows FROM
    t2m_c, surface_pressure_hpa
    ventilation_m2s — blh_m x wind_speed_ms, the standard dispersion-capacity index
  Coverage is 2020-01 to 2026-07, continuous and aligned with `df`.

`profile_df` — pandas DataFrame of ERA5 vertical profiles, one row per station-hour-level,
  timestamps in Beijing local time.
  Columns: datetime, year, month, day, hour, station
    pressure_hpa — 1000, 975, 950, 925, 900, 875, 850 (decreasing pressure = increasing altitude)
    temperature_c, geopotential_height_m
    potential_temperature_k — theta = T(1000/p)^0.286; theta increasing with height
      means the layer is statically stable. A temperature INVERSION — temperature
      itself increasing with height — is a stronger special case, and a layer can
      be stable without being inverted.
  Covers SELECTED MONTHS ONLY; check the available year/month combinations before use.

`cities_df` — hourly city-level observations for 31 cities of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei
  transmission channel (the '2+26' cities plus northern Hebei), 2020-01-01 onward.
  Columns: year, month, day, hour, city (Chinese name), longitude, latitude (city centre),
    PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO_mg_m3, O3, O3_8h, AQI
  NOTE CO here is mg/m3 (column `CO_mg_m3`), unlike the ug/m3 `CO` column of `df`. A city
  value is a municipality-wide network aggregate, not a single station, so it is not directly
  comparable to a `df` station reading.

`aerosol_df` — CAMS EAC4 reanalysis aerosol composition over Beijing, 3-hourly
  (local hours 2, 5, 8, ..., 23), covering 2020-01 to 2025-12 ONLY — seven months
  shorter than the other datasets.
  Columns: datetime, year, month, day, hour
    dust_aod550, black_carbon_aod550, organic_matter_aod550, sulphate_aod550,
      sea_salt_aod550, total_aod550 — aerosol optical depth by species
    dust_fraction — dust_aod550 / total_aod550
    cams_pm2p5_ugm3, cams_pm10_ugm3 — model PM fields (ug/m3)

`fire_df` — pandas DataFrame of daily NASA FIRMS active-fire detections (VIIRS 375 m,
  archive product) relative to central Beijing (116.40E, 39.95N).
  Columns: date, year, month, day
    fires_within_radius, frp_total_mw — all detections within 300 km
    wind_from_deg — daily mean wind direction at Beijing, the direction wind blows FROM
    fires_upwind, frp_upwind_mw — the subset of detections lying within +/-45 degrees
      of the upwind direction

`station_df` — pandas DataFrame with one row per Beijing monitoring station.
  Important columns:
    station, station_name_zh, station_code
    longitude, latitude — benchmark-reproduction coordinates (EPSG:4326)
    registry_longitude, registry_latitude — secondary station-registry references
    coordinate_quality_flag — known provenance or consistency issue
    site_district_name_zh, site_district_code — district associated with the named site
    coordinate_district_name_zh, coordinate_district_code — point-in-polygon result
    district_consistency — whether site identity and coordinate-derived district agree
    network_class_2013 — contemporaneous CEMC urban/suburban class
    functional_role_2013 — urban_assessment, suburban_assessment, or background
    included_in_city_aggregate — false for the Dingling background site
    benchmark_group — AirBench-only group, not an official class
    station_elevation_m — intentionally missing because period-specific elevation is unverified
    terrain_elevation_m — ground-surface elevation (m) sampled from Copernicus DEM GLO-30
      at the benchmark coordinate; this is terrain height, NOT the sampling-inlet
      elevation, and excludes inlet height above ground
    terrain_elevation_status — provenance tag for terrain_elevation_m

Coordinate caveat: use longitude/latitude to reproduce benchmark calculations, but check
coordinate_quality_flag before fine-scale land-use, administrative, or exposure claims. Do
not present registry coordinates as surveyed physical station locations.

WHICH BEIJING. The record offers three of them and a question means the first
unless it names one of the others. (1) The DEFAULT is the twelve-station
network of `df`, every station included, the background site at Dingling among
them. (2) The CITY ASSESSMENT POINTS are the eleven stations flagged
`included_in_city_aggregate`, which excludes Dingling; a question wanting those
says "city assessment points", or names a standard whose own aggregation rule
defines them. (3) The CITY-LEVEL RECORD is Beijing's own row in `cities_df`, a
municipality-wide series published independently of the station network; a
question wanting it says "the city-level record", "the city record" or names
`cities_df`. The three do not agree — dropping Dingling alone moves a network
mean by a few tenths, and the municipal product disagrees with the station
network by more than that — so this is a scored choice, not a formality.

GAS UNITS. Concentrations in this record are mass per volume, in ug/m3 (CO in
the `CO` column likewise, `CO_mg_m3` excepted). A limit or standard quoted in
parts per billion is a MOLE FRACTION and is not on that scale; converting
between the two requires a molar volume, and unless a question says otherwise
this domain uses the reference conditions of 25 degrees Celsius and 1013.25 hPa.

TIMESTAMPS. In the network's air-quality records, `df` and `cities_df`, each row is the
mean over the hour that ENDS at its label: hour 1 is 00:00-01:00 and hour 0 is 23:00-24:00
of the PREVIOUS date, the reading under which the network's own running 8-hour ozone
(`O3_8h`) restarts each day. So a day of air quality is its hours 1 to 23 plus hour 0 of the
next date, and a period named in a question ("2023", "in March", "on 5 May") runs from just
after its first instant to its last instant inclusive. HJ 663-2013's natural day and its
8-hour windows ending 08:00-24:00 are this same day. The reanalysis records (`met_df`,
`profile_df`, `aerosol_df`) are instantaneous values at their stamped time, and a day of
them is its hours 0 to 23; `fire_df` is already daily.

DAILY FIGURES. Unless a question says otherwise, a day's city-wide value for a
quantity is built in two steps: each hour's network figure is the mean over the
stations reporting that hour, and the day's value is the mean of those hourly
network figures over the hours the day reports. This is NOT the same as pooling
the day's station-hours into one mean — station coverage varies within a day,
so the two differ — and a question that names a different construction (a
pooled mean, a per-station daily value, or a standard's own aggregation such as
HJ 633's) overrides this.
</dataset_schema>

<knowledge_base>
Beijing Air Quality Monitoring Network:
- 12 national air quality monitoring stations across Beijing
- Data period: 2020-01-01 to 2026-07-20
- Station classification by location type:
  - Urban core (6): Dongsi, Guanyuan, Wanshouxigong, Tiantan, Nongzhanguan, Aotizhongxin
  - Suburban/rural (4): Changping, Dingling, Huairou, Shunyi
  - Western urban (2): Gucheng, Wanliu
- The three-way grouping above is benchmark-defined. Use `station_df.network_class_2013`
  or `station_df.functional_role_2013` when the question asks for contemporaneous official/network roles.
</knowledge_base>

<examples>
Example 1 - Filter and aggregate:
```python
# Monthly average PM2.5 across all stations; hour 0 closes the previous day, so its month
stamp = pd.to_datetime(df[['year','month','day','hour']])
monthly_pm25 = df.groupby((stamp - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)).dt.month)['PM2.5'].mean()
print(monthly_pm25.round(1))
```

Example 2 - Station comparison:
```python
# Compare urban vs suburban PM2.5
urban = ['Dongsi', 'Guanyuan', 'Wanshouxigong', 'Tiantan', 'Nongzhanguan', 'Aotizhongxin']
suburban = ['Changping', 'Dingling', 'Huairou', 'Shunyi']
urban_avg = df[df['station'].isin(urban)]['PM2.5'].mean()
suburban_avg = df[df['station'].isin(suburban)]['PM2.5'].mean()
print(f"Urban: {{urban_avg:.1f}}, Suburban: {{suburban_avg:.1f}}")
```

Example 3 - Time series with datetime:
```python
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df[['year','month','day','hour']])
# Each hour is labelled by its END: hour 0 closes the previous day.
df['date'] = (df['datetime'] - pd.Timedelta(hours=1)).dt.date
daily = df.groupby(['date', 'station'])['PM2.5'].mean().reset_index()
daily.columns = ['date', 'station', 'daily_pm25']
print(daily.head(10))
```
</examples>
